Inner_Sanctum_movie: Inner Sanctum is a 1948 American horror mystery film directed by Lew Landers and starring Charles Russell and Mary Beth Hughes. based on the Simon & Schuster book series of the same name and the Inner Sanctum Mystery radio series. Morros, Samuel Rheiner and Walter Shenson.

rv: A Taut, Dark Tale - Worthy of Its Radio Show Namesake

Much like the old 1930s radio show of the same name, "Inner Sanctum" offers a taut, dark tale of lies and murder, tinged with just a touch of the paranormal. Charles Russell acquits himself very well as the handsome stranger with a murderous secret hiding out at the local boarding house. Mary Beth Hughes plays one icy ice-blonde, but just how far will she go to protect him? Roscoe Ates is reasonably effective as the boy who knew too much, but his cloying, annoying acting (sadly typical of child actors in this period) is the film's main drawback. Five stars nonetheless for this well-told…

rv: What are the chances of meeting Tex Ritter on a Greyhound?

Even though it has the 'star' power of Tommy Kirk AND Tex Ritter, Freedom Highway isn't as good or delirious as "America For Me" and that somewhat hurts it. Essentially, it follows a LONG Greyhound bus trip from SF to Washington DC, with everyone looking peppy-go-lucky even though they've probably been travelling for days on end. The story follows a number of characters, a boy meeting his troop in Washington, A disgruntled man picking up a congressional medal of honor for his late son, a bit of a laughable love story between a football player and a lady, and a bit of a mystery passenger who's…

I was born this year, 1956. These were typical attitudes of post-WWII America. The movie is obviously meant to support the myths of America and is not meant as realism. A little bite is provided by the disillusioned gentleman who has lost his son in Korea. Reviews of movies from this era tend to be off the mark because people judge them by contemporary standards. They should instead be looked at as time capsules from the past, with warts and all. I can say for certain that 2023 will look terrible 70 years from now, if the US even exists then. The confidence of this era--confidence in…

This, most assuredly, was not MY family. When we went on our road vacations, Dad, still, did 95% of the driving, after Mom got licensed, in 1967. He loved driving! If he was getting a bit tired and, we came to a town with 'iffy-looking' accommodations, we'd press on, to the next. Such wonderful memories, of our car trips!

rv: What happened to the baby that Mary's mom is having at the beginning of the film? You never see him or her and later when we see Mom setting the table (when Lucille is leaving) she's setting the table for only three... Other than that, it's a funny but ironic film. It's naive and innocent and yet current religious right would have big problems with this.

I found this film wonderful, and I cheered (well, quietly lol) when the two finally got together. Best bits: Bob's Mom 'Arranges situations' if no questions about sex came up. How many fucking phases is she going to go through before she's even 17? I sorta fell asleep, and by 10 minutes I was waiting to hear about Mary, now married 30 years, being asked to do "oral" on her now 53 yr old husband no longer interested in missionary position. Whoa! In this film, we mostly see two brothers playing around. whether on the beach, in the snow, playing hockey (there's not a lot of hockey shots in these movies now that I think about it) or in the pool, they're having fun, and ready to horse around for te camera if needed.

customers_wanted: Popeye and Bluto are running competing penny arcades, trying to bring in customer Wimpy. Of course, he would gladly pay Tuesday for a penny today. And of course, their competing arcades show clips featuring each of them, with well over half of this short thus recycled.

rv: The main advantage of this cartoon is it lets you know about old Popeye cartoons that aren't on archive.org yet

I love these old, 1930's era Popeye cartoons, as I've mentioned in several other Popeye reviews. In contrast, if you've watched the 1950's version of them, you immediately see that the 1950's version is far less funny, at least from a verbal point of view. Olive Oyl somehow retained her unbelievably great physical humor, but Popeye and Bluto lost theirs (Bluto also lost that terrific basso profundo voice of his). In addition, a whole host of side characters disappeared (if you have ever seen the Robin Wiiliams movie of Popeye you'll know what I mean). Those are some of the reasons I prefer…

This is the first Popeye I've seen where Wimpy plays a significant role in the story. I'm willing to forgive a plot that serves as a framing device to showcase other episodes to get an insight into this character's... uhm, character. :)
